model: dense GRU H=64, input 6, head 32; Adam 3e-3; batch 128
reading: A dense 64-unit GRU control removes 80-90% of the uniform-baseline error on the theta-posterior target (KL 0.070-0.157 at 1600 updates against baselines 0.757-0.837), so the target is largely learnable in a 64-dimensional state. The residual is above the 0.05 nat headroom scale but the curves are still descending, so this pilot cannot distinguish genuine headroom from undertraining: the registered budget-doubling gate must decide. Note also that the analytic ceiling on the F-X capacity asymmetry is only 0.063 nat, i.e. the same order as the residual, leaving little room for an interaction.
status: engineering pilot; not a verdict; superseded for the gate question by the budget-doubling run
